meta.title: Cerbere Security Shield — Local network protection for Windows
meta.desc: Cerbere Security Shield: free, open-source Windows security suite. Real-time port monitoring, DNS ad/tracker blocking, parental control, firewall hardening, intrusion detection. 100% local, no telemetry.
footer.copy: © 2026 art-qalam-fr — MIT License · Cerbere Security Shield
hero.lead: A Windows security suite that is free, open source and 100% local — network port monitoring, ad and tracker blocking, parental control, firewall hardening and intrusion detection. No telemetry, no cloud, no account.
features.sub: A single dashboard, available in your browser or as a desktop app, keeping an eye on what enters and leaves your machine.
feat1.p: Continuous inventory of listening ports, critical / unexpected / protected classification, global risk score and firewall hardening recommendations.
feat2.p: Local DNS filtering based on EasyList, AdGuard, OISD and HaGeZi lists — automatic updates, live blocking statistics.
feat3.p: Category and per-domain filtering, time slots, daily quotas and access log — protected by an independent PIN.
feat4.p: Audit of exposed ports, automatically generated hardening plan and application of recommended Windows Firewall rules.
feat5.p: Detection of port scans and brute-force attempts, automatic banning of hostile IP addresses, manageable whitelist.
feat6.p: The dashboard can be locked with your Windows session password or a dedicated password — sensitive settings stay protected.
local.sub: Cerbere runs entirely on your machine. Your data goes nowhere.
local.p1: No telemetry, no tracking, no account to create
local.p2: No data sent to any remote server
local.p3: Open and auditable source code under the MIT license
local.p4: Interface translated into French, English, German and Spanish
local.p5: Works in the browser or as a dedicated desktop application
local.p6: System tray icon: protection keeps running in the background
install.sub: One installer, one click, and protection starts.
install.s1: Download the installer via the button above or the GitHub Releases page — CerbereShield_Setup.exe file.
install.s2: Run the installation — Windows may show a SmartScreen warning during the beta phase: More info → Run anyway. Details on the Warnings page.
install.s3: The dashboard opens in your browser or as a desktop app — port monitoring and filtering are active immediately.
home.notice: Beta version. Cerbere Security Shield is in open testing: the application is functional and used daily, but may still contain imperfections. Binaries are signed with a test certificate while our trusted signature is being validated — Windows may therefore show a warning. Learn more: Warnings · Security & privacy.
warn.title: Warnings — Cerbere Security Shield
warn.sub: Read before installing the beta version
warn.beta: Cerbere Security Shield is beta software. It is offered free of charge for testing and evaluation. It is functional and used in real conditions by its authors, but has not yet reached the maturity of a stable release.
warn.s1p1: During the beta phase, binaries are signed with a test certificate (self-signed via SignPath) pending validation of our trusted certificate application with the SignPath Foundation. Windows SmartScreen will therefore probably show:
warn.s1p2: This warning is expected and does not indicate malware: it only means the signing certificate is not yet recognized by SmartScreen reputation. You can verify the file signature (right-click → Properties → Digital Signatures) — the signer must be CN=Cerbere Security Shield, O=art-qalam-fr.
warn.s2li1: Windows 10 or Windows 11, 64-bit only — no macOS or Linux version
warn.s2li2: Administrator rights required for firewall features, local DNS blocking and the intrusion detection service
warn.s2li3: Local port 4050 must be available (dashboard backend)
warn.s2li4: An Internet connection is required only to download blocking-list updates and MalwareBazaar analysis submissions
warn.s3li1: DNS filtering intercepts the machine's DNS requests: some sites may be blocked by the lists (false positives possible). A whitelist lets you lift a block in one click.
warn.s3li2: Firewall hardening creates rules in Windows Firewall. A hardening plan is always shown before application — review it, some rules may cut legitimate uses (network sharing, local servers, online games).
warn.s3li3: Intrusion detection may automatically ban IP addresses; bans are reversible from the Intrusion Detection tab.
warn.s3li4: Parental control restricts access to site categories for the configured profile — keep the PIN safe: it also protects disabling the filter.
warn.s4p: Like any security software that touches the firewall, DNS and processes, Cerbere may be flagged by some antiviruses — especially since binaries are not yet signed with a trusted certificate. The source code is fully public on GitHub: you can audit it or compile the application yourself.
warn.s5p: The software is provided “as is”, under the MIT license, without warranty of any kind. The authors cannot be held liable for damage, data loss or service interruption resulting from its use — particularly firewall rules or DNS filtering. In beta, preferably test on a non-critical machine.
warn.bug: Found a bug? Open an issue on GitHub Issues.
warn.summary: Summary. Beta = expected SmartScreen warning + admin rights required + features that touch the network. If you are not comfortable with that, wait for the stable version — or read the Security & privacy page to understand exactly what the application does (and does not do).
sec.title: Security & privacy — Cerbere Security Shield
sec.sub: What Cerbere does, what it does not do, and how releases are signed
sec.modelp: Cerbere Security Shield is an entirely local application. The backend listens on localhost:4050 and only accepts local origins (browser on the machine, embedded desktop app). No port is exposed outward by the application.
sec.ml1: Optional application lock: Windows session or dedicated password (salted hash, never stored in clear). Modification actions require an unlocked session.
sec.ml2: PIN-protected parental control independent from the main lock.
sec.ml3: External traffic limited to the strict minimum: downloading public block lists (EasyList, AdGuard, OISD, HaGeZi) and hash queries to MalwareBazaar (abuse.ch — free, no key). No other external API, no paid key, no third-party service.
sec.ml4: Links to VirusTotal, ProcessLibrary, SpeedGuide or SANS ISC are simple navigation links — no data is automatically sent to them.
sec.privp: Cerbere Security Shield collects no personal data. Concretely:
sec.pl1: No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reporting to an external server.
sec.pl2: No user account, no registration, no tracking cookie.
sec.pl3: All data (configuration, logs, protection state, lists) is stored locally on your machine.
sec.pl4: The only outbound requests concern public resources: block lists (read-only download) and MalwareBazaar (sending a file hash for reputation analysis — never the file itself).
sec.pl5: The website sets no cookie and loads no third-party resource.
sec.privq: For any privacy-related question: open an issue on GitHub Issues.
sec.signp: Official binaries are produced exclusively by the CI/CD pipeline of the public repository art-qalam-fr/CerbereShield (GitHub Actions) and signed via SignPath.io.
sec.sl1: Each signature is submitted through a dedicated signing request per release — no silent automatic signing.
sec.sl2: During beta, the certificate used is a self-signed test certificate (CN=Cerbere Security Shield, O=art-qalam-fr, OU=Open Source). Once our application with the SignPath Foundation is approved, releases will be signed with a publicly trusted certificate.
sec.sl3: Verifying a signature: right-click the exe → Properties → Digital Signatures. The signer name must match the project's official certificate.
sec.sl4: Team: project maintained by the art-qalam-fr organization (single author; the Author / Reviewer / Approver roles are held by the maintainer, signing requests are reviewed manually).
sec.signnote: Code signing for this open-source project is provided by the SignPath Foundation via SignPath.io.
sec.vulnp: Have you identified a security issue? Please do not publish the exploit publicly before a fix. Open an issue on GitHub Issues with the [security] prefix — stating the version, platform and reproduction steps.
sec.tl3: The application can be recompiled from sources for independent verification.

about.title: About us — Cerbere Security Shield
about.mdesc: Why Cerbere Security Shield exists: a tool born from a personal need for network visibility, released as open source for everyone.
about.sub: The story behind the project, the mindset, and why open source
about.s1: A personal need turned into a public tool
about.s1p1: Cerbere Security Shield was not born from a business plan, but from a concrete need. As a self-taught developer, I use modern tools daily — MCP servers, local services, development agents — that open many ports on my machine. It quickly became essential for me to observe and control what enters and leaves: which ports are listening, which DNS requests go out, which processes communicate.
about.s1p2: Rather than stacking utilities, I built the tool I was looking for — then decided to make it public, because this need is not mine alone.
about.s2p1: Most blockers work as black boxes: they filter by default without showing what actually passes — and some deliberately leave doors open to partners who fund them (“acceptable” ads, disguised tracking). Cerbere takes the opposite bet: every DNS request going in or out is visible, filterable and documented, interactively, without leaving the application.
about.s2p2: You concretely see what Windows does in the background — telemetry, commercial tracking, unexpected calls — and you take back control. Control is not delegated: it returns to you.
about.s3: Honesty about the state of the project
about.s3p1: Cerbere fulfils its functions daily, but it is not a finished product: some areas — intrusion detection in particular — are still being hardened. The application is distributed free of charge, as is, under the MIT license: security is everyone's business, and the author cannot be held liable for any flaws it may still contain.
about.s3p2: Test, audit, report bugs — every piece of feedback improves the version.
about.s4p1: A security tool must be inspectable — that is the bare minimum for software that touches the network. Beyond transparency, open source carries the project's values: sharing, mutual aid, collective improvement. The code is public, auditable, and recompilable by anyone who wants to verify what they install.
about.s5p1: The project lives on GitHub. Developers: your help is welcome — fixes, features, code review. Testers: your bug reports are precious — please be kind, this project is the work of one person, not a team.
about.s6p1: This site and this software also serve as a showcase: they concretely show what one person can build end to end — backend, interface, packaging, multilingual distribution. If this work resonates with your projects, if you are looking for a development partner or a profile that learns fast and delivers a complete product, contact me via GitHub — I am open to collaborations as well as professional opportunities.
donate.title: Support the project — Cerbere Security Shield
donate.mdesc: Cerbere is free and will never sell your data. Support the project with a donation: code signing, testing, development.
donate.sub: Cerbere is free and always will be — donations fund what genuinely costs money
donate.stance: Cerbere sells nothing and will never sell your data — it collects none anyway: everything stays on your machine. The project is free, open source, and carried by a single person. Donations don't pay for code: they pay for what an independent developer cannot produce for free.
donate.c1p: A signing certificate removes SmartScreen warnings and proves the installer hasn't been tampered with — the project's biggest expense.
donate.c2p: Testing the installer, DNS filtering and intrusion detection across varied configurations requires dedicated hardware and test environments.
donate.c3p: Hardening intrusion detection, fixes, translations, answering bug reports — a security project must stay actively maintained.
donate.secure_paypal: Secure payment via PayPal — credit card accepted, no PayPal account needed
donate.thanks: Every donation, however small, has a direct impact — and remains entirely optional, of course. Thank you for keeping the project alive.
